# Reader discovery on real disk — 2026-11-04

This separate L4/N4 observation record changes no runtime behavior and establishes neither a speed-up nor an SLO. The older [tmpfs matrix](reader-discovery-latency-2026-10-23.md), clarified in `dc637c324d680fe8931034265d08f9f2d578b0fc`, used standalone reader batches and is not a measurement of this wiring.

## Source and environment

- Fixed measured source SHA: `fb19abf637618dba11e99cd28ea4c0e2ebe0e340` (assigned origin/develop head).
- Host: `dev`, `Linux-7.3.1-1-cachyos-x86_64-with-glibc2.44`; CPU `AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX 16-Core Processor`.
- Toolchain: `rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13)`.
- Managed root: `/home/fujimogn/.cache/herdr-lineup-reader-n4`; task ID `asg-reader-discovery-n4`.
- Diagnostic measurement run work directory: `/home/fujimogn/.cache/herdr-lineup-reader-n4/runs/19be6b974430af8d44fef118293ac50a/work`.
- Three runs' apparent bytes at matrix measurement end (before the later probe): 2120735335, below 5,000,000,000 bytes.

```text
SOURCE    FSTYPE TARGET
/dev/sda2 ext4   /
```

Source copies, build outputs and every synthetic candidate fixture are below a managed run on `/dev/sda2` ext4, not tmpfs. Storage placement does not imply device I/O on each lookup.

## Protocol, reproducibility and isolation

Start with `dev-task-temp run --root /home/fujimogn/.cache/herdr-lineup-reader-n4 --task-id asg-reader-discovery-n4 --bytes 5000000000 --inodes 100000 -- python3 -`. The Python parent archives the fixed SHA with `git archive --format=zip`, extracts tracked files into `$DEV_TASK_TEMP_DIR/source`, and directs Cargo to `$DEV_TASK_TEMP_DIR/target`. It sets `RUSTC_WRAPPER=''`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4`, `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0`, `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0`. For this diagnostic run only, dependency build artifacts were copied from the second failed run to the new run; the modified library and test were rebuilt. No tracked Rust in the dedicated worktree was edited.

To avoid Unix socket address length limits, the parent opens `$DEV_TASK_TEMP_DIR/t` and exports `/proc/<parent-pid>/fd/<fd>` as TMPDIR while it waits for Cargo. This is a short path into the same ext4 run. The mock socket similarly uses `/proc/self/fd/<fd>/s`, resolving into each coordinate's run-owned state directory. All processes remain inside the supervisor command tree. The bytes argument is a capacity request, not an enforced runtime quota; total apparent bytes were checked separately.

Insert the complete harness below immediately before the final brace of the existing `publish::tests` module. Apply the two exact logging insertions shown below in this disposable copy. Then execute:

```sh
cargo test --release --locked --lib publish::tests::real_disk_reader_matrix_n4 -- --ignored --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1
```

The existing test helpers `budget_server`, `budget_template`, `budget_pane`, and `budget_workspace` supply synthetic snapshots and mock acknowledgments over a private Unix socket. No Herdr executable or user server/session is contacted. Explicit synthetic Homes replace user agent home paths; no user `~/.codex`, `~/.kimi` or credentials are read. Network access stays disabled; no user settings are changed.

Each provider is measured independently: Codex candidate counts 10/100/500/1500/3000 and Kimi 10/50/100/500/1500, each crossed with panes 1/4/8/16/32. Each of the 50 coordinates has 5 warmups and 50 measured repetitions: 2,750 refreshes, 2,500 measured samples. Pane i reuses session i % candidates when panes exceed candidates. Counts include matched candidates. Codex uses uncompressed rollout files under sessions/2026/11/04; Kimi counts state.json candidates under sessions/wd_synthetic/<id>, each accompanied by a main-agent wire file. All payloads are small synthetic valid observations.

Each iteration calls actual `refresh_with_readers_inner`, which constructs one diagnostics-bearing ReadCycle shared across panes, and actual bounded Codex/Kimi readers. `reader_ns` sums the existing Instant intervals around reader.read_in_cycle, including discovery, validation, tail parsing, cache checks, worker scheduling and caller wait. It excludes snapshot, Git, socket, checkpoint, report work and post-call logging/worker-release checks. Rare fallback diagnostics are emitted inside the timer and can perturb it. It is not discovery-only CPU time or end-to-end latency. Workspace checkout is absent, avoiding Git children.

Each coordinate retains its publisher across iterations; every refresh starts a new ReadCycle. Provider caches persist in one process. Fixtures are created once per candidate-count group. There is no cache drop, forced fsync-before-read, randomized ordering or cold-device protocol: these are warm page-cache observations in provider/candidate/pane ascending order. Other builds were observed running concurrently; host load was not controlled. The default 2-second reader timeout is retained; max observation age is 24 hours. Attempts/completions, BUSY, deadline and worker failure assertions are retained. Availability is observed, not required. Raw reader results are collected after the reader timer and before publisher timeout restoration; `final_available` separately reports available cached publisher readings.

## Main table

Kimi's 1500-candidate rows measure entry-limit refusal, not successful usage discovery. This fixture has one working-directory entry, 1500 session-directory entries, and two entries (state.json and agents) inside each session directory: 4501 entries in a complete traversal. The existing budget stops at entry 4097. All 3050 measured calls and all 305 warmup calls at that candidate count returned Unavailable(EntryLimit), across all five pane counts. The smaller Kimi coordinates and all Codex coordinates returned available context on every call. This is the specified entry-cap behavior, not evidence of a new runtime defect. Candidate count and traversal-entry count are different quantities.

All duration statistics include every measured refresh, including ones with missing context. Milliseconds, median as average of middle values, p95 nearest rank (sorted value 48/50). Missing denominator is actual reader calls (panes × 50), and reasons refer to raw context UsageOutcome. Warmup missing counts (panes × 5 denominator) are separate. Total measured missing calls: 3050.

## Fallback diagnostics

Captured inside the unchanged cumulative-budget fallback branch. `entries` is the budget already consumed before fallback; `changed` reports ancestor/directory stamps differing at the diagnostic observation. The diagnostic recheck occurs after the branch condition, so an additional transient change can affect the list.

```text
N4_FALLBACK,entries=1503,changed=["/home/fujimogn"]
```

## Earlier failures and missing-context investigation

Run 735ecd670346fcb6c797b3cee95dbef4 passed fmt and Clippy but ordinary tests failed (375 passed, 68 failed, 6 ignored), including `path must be shorter than SUN_LEN`; no measurements ran. The second run 003d6e92c6eb6684a90e95b5d52ce7f9 used short TMPDIR and passed the five mandatory checks on the unmodified fixed archive: fmt, strict locked all-target Clippy, cargo test --locked (443 unit + 1 integration passed, 6 ignored), cargo build --release --locked, and release binary --help. Its added measurement aborted at Codex 3000 candidates / 8 panes, measured iteration 47: local_readings was 7, expected 8. Attempts/completions and zero BUSY/deadline/worker failure checks had passed. That run did not record raw UsageOutcome, so its exact historical MissingReason cannot be recovered from the available evidence. Its partial samples are excluded from this matrix. The diagnostic rerun above records every outcome, rather than hiding missing observations or assuming the historical reason.

The fixed source's ReadCycle records all home ancestors and traversed directories. A stamp change during initial traversal triggers a second full traversal under the remaining cumulative budget. At 3000 Codex candidates plus three directory entries, a second traversal exceeds the 4096 entry cap. EntryLimit on that path is specified fail-closed behavior, independent of the caller's completed-worker diagnostic. An unrelated update to an ancestor can trigger the fallback. Any assignment of that reason to the earlier uninstrumented iteration is an inference, not a direct observation; evidence and unresolved classification are stated separately in the final verification below.

The failed payloads remain protected. The new run is retained as well; only the commander may decide reclaim after ACK. No runtime fix is included.

## Source verification and limits

SHA-256 of fixed unmodified src/publish.rs: `25cde899a4e9fd275a522e550c4dc7d4283273bdced9a6e37afa1a85047a8529`. The full run produced all 50 coordinates with 5 warmups and 50 measured repetitions each; table values were computed from its raw samples. The diagnostic test command exited 0. Source checks above apply to the exact unmodified fixed SHA; only the full additions shown below were applied afterward.

One Linux host/ext4 mount, synthetic small files, warm caches and uncontrolled concurrent load. Logging and test-only reader gates add overhead. No macOS, network filesystem, compressed rollout, cold-device guarantee, mutation matrix, live Herdr latency or stuck-worker frequency was measured. Publisher activity between panes can affect scheduling. Historical tmpfs results used a different commit and standalone readers, so no improvement comparison is supported.

Full addition inside publish::tests:

```rust

    thread_local! {
        pub(super) static N4_OUTCOMES: std::cell::RefCell<Vec<(String, model::UsageOutcome)>> = const { std::cell::RefCell::new(Vec::new()) };
    }
    // Measurement-only addition in a disposable copy; never shipped.
    #[test]
    #[ignore]
    fn real_disk_reader_matrix_n4() {
        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
        let root = PathBuf::from(std::env::var_os("DEV_TASK_TEMP_DIR").unwrap());
        println!("N4_HEADER,provider,candidates,panes,iteration,reader_ns,attempts,completed");
        for provider in ["codex", "kimi"] {
            let counts: &[usize] = if provider == "codex" { &[10,100,500,1500,3000] } else { &[10,50,100,500,1500] };
            for &candidates in counts {
                let home = root.join(format!("fixtures/{provider}-{candidates}"));
                std::fs::create_dir_all(&home).unwrap();
                let now_ms = SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_millis();
                let timestamp = "2026-11-04T10:27:46Z";
                for index in 0..candidates {
                    let id = format!("synthetic-{index}");
                    if provider == "codex" {
                        let dir = home.join("sessions/2026/11/04");
                        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
                        let meta = json!({"type":"session_meta","payload":{"id":id}});
                        let event = json!({"type":"event_msg","timestamp":timestamp,"payload":{"type":"token_count","info":{"last_token_usage":{"total_tokens":26000},"model_context_window":212000}}});
                        std::fs::write(dir.join(format!("rollout-{index}-{id}.jsonl")),format!("{meta}\n{event}\n")).unwrap();
                    } else {
                        let dir = home.join("sessions/wd_synthetic").join(&id);
                        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("agents/main")).unwrap();
                        std::fs::write(dir.join("state.json"),json!({"id":id,"cwd":"/synthetic/repo","title":"synthetic"}).to_string()).unwrap();
                        let metadata = json!({"type":"metadata","protocol_version":"1.5","created_at":1});
                        let bind = json!({"type":"profile.bind","agentId":"main","modelAlias":"synthetic-alias","systemPrompt":"synthetic","disallowedTools":[],"thinkingEffort":"off","time":now_ms});
                        let turn = json!({"type":"token_counting.turn_recorded","agentId":"main","turnId":1,"length":2,"tokens":75,"time":now_ms});
                        std::fs::write(dir.join("agents/main/wire.jsonl"),format!("{metadata}\n{bind}\n{turn}\n")).unwrap();
                    }
                }
                if provider == "kimi" {
                    std::fs::write(home.join("config.toml"),"[models.\"synthetic-alias\"]\nmax_input_size = 1000\nmax_context_size = 100000\n").unwrap();
                }
                for panes in [1usize,4,8,16,32] {
                    let state = root.join(format!("state/{provider}-{candidates}-{panes}"));
                    std::fs::create_dir_all(&state).unwrap();
                    let fd = File::open(&state).unwrap();
                    let socket = PathBuf::from(format!("/proc/self/fd/{}/s",fd.as_raw_fd()));
                    let pane_values = (0..panes).map(|i| {
                        let mut p = budget_pane(&format!("w1:p{i}"),"w1",Some(provider),&format!("synthetic-{}",i%candidates));
                        p["cwd"] = json!("/synthetic/repo"); p
                    }).collect();
                    let template = budget_template(pane_values, vec![budget_workspace("w1",None)]);
                    let server = budget_server(UnixListener::bind(&socket).unwrap(),template,BudgetServer::default(),BudgetLog::default());
                    let mut transport = Transport::connect(&socket).unwrap();
                    let homes = Homes {codex:Some(home.clone()),kimi:Some(home.clone()),..Homes::default()};
                    let mut publisher = MetadataPublisher::new(state,"fake".into(),homes).unwrap();
                    let config = Config { usage_max_age_ms:86400000, ..Config::default() };
                    let diagnostic_provider = if provider=="codex" {model::Provider::Codex} else {model::Provider::Kimi};
                    for iteration in 0..55usize {
                        publisher.reset_stages();
                        N4_OUTCOMES.with(|v| v.borrow_mut().clear());
                        publisher.refresh_with_readers_inner(&mut transport,&config,&CodexReader,&GrokReader).unwrap();
                        let ns=publisher.stages.lock().unwrap().as_ref().unwrap().reader.as_nanos();
                        let until=Instant::now()+Duration::from_secs(1);
                        let diag=loop {
                            if let Ok(d)=publisher.reader_diagnostics.snapshot(diagnostic_provider) {
                                if !d.worker_active {break d;}
                            }
                            assert!(Instant::now()<until); std::thread::yield_now();
                        };
                        assert_eq!(diag.attempts,(panes*(iteration+1)) as u64);
                        assert_eq!(diag.completed,diag.attempts);
                        assert_eq!(diag.busy_rejections,0);
                        assert_eq!(diag.deadline_ends,0);
                        assert_eq!(diag.worker_failures,0);
                        let outcomes=N4_OUTCOMES.with(|v|v.borrow().clone());
                        assert_eq!(outcomes.len(),panes);
                        let available=outcomes.iter().filter(|(_,o)|matches!(o,model::UsageOutcome::Available(_))).count();
                        let final_available=publisher.local_readings.values().filter(|r|matches!(r.context,model::UsageOutcome::Available(_))).count();
                        let details=outcomes.iter().map(|(id,o)|format!("{id}:{o:?}")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(";");
                        let phase=if iteration<5 {"warmup"} else {"measured"};
                        let index=if iteration<5 {iteration} else {iteration-5};
                        println!("N4,{provider},{candidates},{panes},{phase},{index},{ns},{available},{},{final_available},{},{},{details}",panes-available,diag.attempts,diag.completed);
                    }
                    publisher.request(&mut transport,"test.finish").unwrap();
                    server.join().unwrap();
                }
            }
        }
    }

```

For a separate clean archived copy, use the full probe harness below instead of the matrix harness (do not combine their duplicate N4_OUTCOMES definitions). The two logging insertions are identical to the matrix additions above; no other source modification is made.

```rust

    thread_local! {
        pub(super) static N4_OUTCOMES: std::cell::RefCell<Vec<(String, model::UsageOutcome)>> = const { std::cell::RefCell::new(Vec::new()) };
    }
    // Measurement-only addition in a disposable copy; never shipped.
    #[test]
    #[ignore]
    fn real_disk_reader_probe_n4() {
        use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
        let root = PathBuf::from(std::env::var_os("DEV_TASK_TEMP_DIR").unwrap());
        println!("N4_HEADER,provider,candidates,panes,iteration,reader_ns,attempts,completed");
        for provider in ["codex"] {
            let counts: &[usize] = &[3000];
            for &candidates in counts {
                let home = root.join(format!("fixtures/{provider}-{candidates}"));
                std::fs::create_dir_all(&home).unwrap();
                let now_ms = SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_millis();
                let timestamp = "2026-11-04T10:32:22Z";
                for index in 0..candidates {
                    let id = format!("synthetic-{index}");
                    if provider == "codex" {
                        let dir = home.join("sessions/2026/11/04");
                        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
                        let meta = json!({"type":"session_meta","payload":{"id":id}});
                        let event = json!({"type":"event_msg","timestamp":timestamp,"payload":{"type":"token_count","info":{"last_token_usage":{"total_tokens":26000},"model_context_window":212000}}});
                        std::fs::write(dir.join(format!("rollout-{index}-{id}.jsonl")),format!("{meta}\n{event}\n")).unwrap();
                    } else {
                        let dir = home.join("sessions/wd_synthetic").join(&id);
                        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("agents/main")).unwrap();
                        std::fs::write(dir.join("state.json"),json!({"id":id,"cwd":"/synthetic/repo","title":"synthetic"}).to_string()).unwrap();
                        let metadata = json!({"type":"metadata","protocol_version":"1.5","created_at":1});
                        let bind = json!({"type":"profile.bind","agentId":"main","modelAlias":"synthetic-alias","systemPrompt":"synthetic","disallowedTools":[],"thinkingEffort":"off","time":now_ms});
                        let turn = json!({"type":"token_counting.turn_recorded","agentId":"main","turnId":1,"length":2,"tokens":75,"time":now_ms});
                        std::fs::write(dir.join("agents/main/wire.jsonl"),format!("{metadata}\n{bind}\n{turn}\n")).unwrap();
                    }
                }
                if provider == "kimi" {
                    std::fs::write(home.join("config.toml"),"[models.\"synthetic-alias\"]\nmax_input_size = 1000\nmax_context_size = 100000\n").unwrap();
                }
                for panes in [8usize] {
                    let state = root.join(format!("state/{provider}-{candidates}-{panes}"));
                    std::fs::create_dir_all(&state).unwrap();
                    let fd = File::open(&state).unwrap();
                    let socket = PathBuf::from(format!("/proc/self/fd/{}/s",fd.as_raw_fd()));
                    let pane_values = (0..panes).map(|i| {
                        let mut p = budget_pane(&format!("w1:p{i}"),"w1",Some(provider),&format!("synthetic-{}",i%candidates));
                        p["cwd"] = json!("/synthetic/repo"); p
                    }).collect();
                    let template = budget_template(pane_values, vec![budget_workspace("w1",None)]);
                    let server = budget_server(UnixListener::bind(&socket).unwrap(),template,BudgetServer::default(),BudgetLog::default());
                    let mut transport = Transport::connect(&socket).unwrap();
                    let homes = Homes {codex:Some(home.clone()),kimi:Some(home.clone()),..Homes::default()};
                    let mut publisher = MetadataPublisher::new(state,"fake".into(),homes).unwrap();
                    let config = Config { usage_max_age_ms:86400000, ..Config::default() };
                    let diagnostic_provider = if provider=="codex" {model::Provider::Codex} else {model::Provider::Kimi};
                    for iteration in 0..205usize {
                        publisher.reset_stages();
                        N4_OUTCOMES.with(|v| v.borrow_mut().clear());
                        publisher.refresh_with_readers_inner(&mut transport,&config,&CodexReader,&GrokReader).unwrap();
                        let ns=publisher.stages.lock().unwrap().as_ref().unwrap().reader.as_nanos();
                        let until=Instant::now()+Duration::from_secs(1);
                        let diag=loop {
                            if let Ok(d)=publisher.reader_diagnostics.snapshot(diagnostic_provider) {
                                if !d.worker_active {break d;}
                            }
                            assert!(Instant::now()<until); std::thread::yield_now();
                        };
                        assert_eq!(diag.attempts,(panes*(iteration+1)) as u64);
                        assert_eq!(diag.completed,diag.attempts);
                        assert_eq!(diag.busy_rejections,0);
                        assert_eq!(diag.deadline_ends,0);
                        assert_eq!(diag.worker_failures,0);
                        let outcomes=N4_OUTCOMES.with(|v|v.borrow().clone());
                        assert_eq!(outcomes.len(),panes);
                        let available=outcomes.iter().filter(|(_,o)|matches!(o,model::UsageOutcome::Available(_))).count();
                        let final_available=publisher.local_readings.values().filter(|r|matches!(r.context,model::UsageOutcome::Available(_))).count();
                        let details=outcomes.iter().map(|(id,o)|format!("{id}:{o:?}")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(";");
                        let phase=if iteration<5 {"warmup"} else {"measured"};
                        let index=if iteration<5 {iteration} else {iteration-5};
                        println!("N4,{provider},{candidates},{panes},{phase},{index},{ns},{available},{},{final_available},{},{},{details}",panes-available,diag.attempts,diag.completed);
                    }
                    publisher.request(&mut transport,"test.finish").unwrap();
                    server.join().unwrap();
                }
            }
        }
    }

```


## Final factual verification and retained storage

Independent verification parsed both CSV blocks (2750 matrix rows and 205 probe rows), checked every per-call outcome count and cumulative attempts/completions, recalculated all 50 table rows (median, nearest-rank p95, mean, min, max and missing rates), and checked the 200-probe summary. The measured SHA and source SHA-256 were matched against Git, and `git diff -- src` in the dedicated worktree was empty. UTF-8/LF and whitespace checks passed. The five source-check logs are `check-0.log` through `check-4.log` under failed run 003d6e92c6eb6684a90e95b5d52ce7f9/work (fmt, Clippy, test, release build, help respectively); the later measurement failure does not undo those earlier command exit statuses. Primary logs outside this repository remain subject to commander verification.

Only EntryLimit missing outcomes were observed in the completed matrix; none occurred in the separate 200 measured probe repetitions. The matrix's single fallback logged entries=1503 and a changed /home/fujimogn ancestor, without causing a missing result. There is no observed out-of-spec MissingReason in these completed runs. The original 7/8 event's reason remains unknown; attributing it to fallback EntryLimit remains a hypothesis. Commander note note_m1b_limit authorized closing the observation item with this limit stated. The existing passing test model::tests::cycle_discovery_fallback_keeps_consumed_entries_and_original_deadline separately verifies cumulative-budget refusal; it does not identify that original event.
